== Biography ==
=== Current father assessment, 23 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow, the Edinburgh weaver]] is assessed as son of [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow of the Duddingston account]] at 91% confident inference, increased from the recorded 86% probable. The 1641 apprenticeship expressly names Robert as James’s father and supplies the Wester Duddingston association. The 1649 burgess entry repeats William Sclaitter and the exact 16 June 1641 apprenticeship date, securely identifying that son as the Edinburgh weaver [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]]. The indexed Robert Glasgow burial in the same parish on 17 January 1647 is a coherent match to that father six years later. No positively evidenced competing Duddingston Robert has emerged from the held family comparisons. [[Glasgow-1027|Robert Glasgow]] is a Glasgow cordiner with proved parents but no held Duddingston connection; [[Glasgow-4006|Robert Glasgow]] is a possible earlier identity of this adult, not evidence of a second local father. Together these positive identity and locality links warrant 91% confident inference rather than retaining a probable ceiling solely for an unattested namesake possibility. The father’s identification with the burial account remains inferred, not a direct statement joining those records. The burial index supplies no age, occupation, wife, child or precise residence; parish burial alone does not prove residence at Wester Duddingston. The burgess entry corroborates James’s identity, not an independent father statement. The placement of “servitor” in the printed apprenticeship remains ambiguous. No numerical surname-rarity claim is made. A different local Robert remains possible, and the original burial is still uninspected. This regrades the existing [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow]] to [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]] pair only, from 86% probable to 91% confident inference. It names no new father. Robert’s own [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow]] father hypothesis stays 28%; Elizat’s and Deborah’s maternal conclusions are unchanged. The Duffe adult identification remains 70% and [[Glasgow-2682|James Glasgow]]’s conditional Robert father remains 61%; these subjective nested assessments are not recalculated by multiplication. All people, life dates and other family links remain separate.

This supersedes earlier 86% or probable wording for this exact older-James pair. The historical dated arguments are retained; the later Duffe account’s 61% remains unreviewed in this reassessment.

'''James Glasgow''' was born before 16 June 1641, probably in Scotland. His precise date and place of birth have not been identified.

He became a weaver and burgess of Edinburgh.

=== Apprenticeship and burgess status ===

On 16 June 1641 James, explicitly described as a son of '''Robert Glasgow, servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston''', was apprenticed to William Sclaitter, weaver.<ref name="Apprentice1641">Francis J. Grant, ed., ''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1583–1666'' (Scottish Record Society, 1906), printed p. 71, [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up scan]: “Glasgow, James, son to Robert G., servitor to William Crichtoun, in Wester Duddingston, with William Sclaitter, weaver 16 June 1641.”</ref>

James was admitted as a burgess of Edinburgh on 20 June 1649. The entry identifies him as a weaver, states that he had been apprenticed to the deceased William Sklatter, and repeats the apprenticeship date of 16 June 1641.<ref name="Burgess1649">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 208: “Glasgow, James, B., weiver, as p. to umq. Wm. Sklaitter, weiver, B. (16 June 1641) 20 June 1649.”</ref>

The matching master and exact apprenticeship date establish that the 1641 apprentice was the later Edinburgh weaver and burgess.

=== Marriages ===

James married first '''[[Whyte-2772|Bessie Whyte]]''' at Edinburgh on 6 July 1649.<ref name="EdinburghMarriages">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 267: “Glasgow, James, weaver; Bessie Whyte 6 July 1649” and “James, weaver; Agnes Duncan 11 Nov. 1653.”</ref>

He married second '''[[Duncan-16106|Agnes Duncan]]''' at Edinburgh on 11 November 1653.<ref name="EdinburghMarriages" />

The matching name, occupation and parish, together with the sequential dates, identify the bridegroom in both entries as the same James Glasgow.

=== Children ===

James's known children were:

* '''[[Glasgow-3097|Helen Glasgow]]''', daughter of Bessie Whyte;
* '''[[Glasgow-3099|Jonet Glasgow]]''', daughter of Bessie Whyte;
* '''[[Glasgow-1374|Robert Glasgow]]''', son of Agnes Duncan;<ref name="RobertBaptism">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRSV-T1T Robert Glasgow, baptised 5 May 1655, Edinburgh], son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.</ref>
* '''[[Glasgow-3143|Marion Glasgow]]''', daughter of Agnes Duncan;
* '''[[Glasgow-1373|Bethia Glasgow]]''', daughter of Agnes Duncan; and
* '''[[Glasgow-1057|John Glasgow]]''', son of Agnes Duncan.

The individual baptismal records should be consulted for the evidence identifying each child's mother.

Marion Glasgow married William Calder at Edinburgh on 29 June 1686.<ref name="MarionMarriage">Henry Paton, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278 ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of Edinburgh, 1595–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1905), printed p. 268: “Glasgow, Marion; William Calder 29 June 1686.”</ref>

On the following day William Calder was admitted as a burgess through his wife Marion, who was explicitly described as a daughter of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess.<ref name="CalderBurgess">Charles B. Boog Watson, ed., [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=101 ''Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses and Guild-Brethren, 1406–1700''] (Scottish Record Society, 1929), printed p. 91: “Calder, Wm., B., weaver, be r. of w. Marion, dr. to James Glasgow, weaver, B. 30 June 1686.”</ref>

This directly establishes Marion as James's daughter.

James's date and place of death have not been identified. The maintained master-apprentice records place him alive on 18 October 1693; their full citations are retained below.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current Edinburgh older-weaver identity and ancestry — 21 October 2026 ===

James [[Glasgow-2682]], father of the Edinburgh Duffe household, probably represents the same adult as James [[Glasgow-1150]], the weaver apprenticed on 16 June 1641 and admitted burgess on 20 June 1649: 70% subjective identity confidence. The 1696 James and 1699 youngest-son Thomas apprenticeships name a father James Glasgow, weaver and burgess of Edinburgh. Thomas’s maintained 1684 baptismal identification and the Duffe household’s James children of 1679 and 1680 fit those apprenticeship ages and the youngest-son order. The older craftsman independently has that specific craft and civic status, with an exact master/date cross-reference between his 1641 apprenticeship and 1649 admission. The maintained admission review found one matching admission, although this does not establish uniqueness. His marriages to Bessie Whyte on 6 July 1649 and Agnes Duncan on 11 November 1653, followed by Agnes’s burial as the weaver’s wife on 21 January 1674, permit a later Duffe household beginning in 1677. Successive marriages explain the wife sequence without requiring another same-name weaver and burgess.

Select Robert [[Glasgow-1156]] as James-2682’s probable working father at 61%, conditional on that preferred adult identity and the existing 86% identification of the 1641 apprentice’s named father Robert with the Duddingston account buried in 1647. This replaces only the former local Johnne [[Glasgow-1151]] hypothesis, retained unselected at 26%. The live father was blank in the public check on 21 October 2026: the outstanding WikiTree action is a new probable father addition, not replacement of a live father. The 61% and 70% are subjective assessments of nested propositions, not independent confirmations or statistically calculated probabilities.

The main weaknesses are a very long working life and late fatherhood through 1691, together with the absence of a marriage, prior-wife clause, address, witness or admission-date reference directly joining the Duffe husband to the 1649 burgess. The 1693 same-name weaver master is an inferred identification, not an independently dated identity bridge. Another younger Edinburgh weaver and burgess remains possible. The cancelled 1690 Lindsayland apprenticeship could concern the 1696 son, but its deceased father would conflict with assigning that father to the living 1693 master; resolve this before a merge. Retain both James profiles as accounts of potentially one adult, not two proved sons of Robert. Johnne-1151 remains an unselected younger-family alternative at 26%, alongside the James-3076/James-3077 and Annapill Glessie childhood route, John-1084’s Gordon family, and an unrecorded father. Those alternatives are conditional on the Duffe husband being a distinct younger man, not equally compatible with the preferred pre-1641 adult.

The circa-1655 birth, previously inferred from the first known child in 1677, is a creation estimate rather than an age or birth record. The preferred older-adult identity independently supports birth before 16 June 1641, uncertain and conditional on that identity. Replace the local preferred estimate with that boundary, retaining the old circa-1655 and “by about 1657” reasoning as superseded history. This is a separate vital/identity correction, not a date altered solely to fit Robert’s 1647 burial. No exact birth year is established; retain the broad Midlothian birthplace without claiming a new birthplace record.

No mother is selected for James-2682; do not transfer Deborah Ivey or any wife of Robert from the older profile. Robert’s own 28% Corsoun father hypothesis and the older James’s 86% Robert link are unchanged. The 1696 apprentice’s selected father James-2682 remains 82%, probable mother [[Duffe-18]] remains 72%, and brother comparison remains 79%. The two childhood James accounts stay separate. This is a reassessment of held evidence, with no new source discovery, original inspection, profile merger, live edit or confident upgrade. Connectivity counts still describe retained profile accounts and cannot establish their distinctness.

The most useful test is an Edinburgh marriage, guild, property, witness or prior-wife clause linking the Duffe husband to the 1649 burgess. Check the original 1690 cancelled indenture against the 1693 master before identifying that son or merging either James account; inspect the original Duffe baptisms for residence and witnesses. These are targeted next tests, not prerequisites to representing the preferred probable family.<ref name="EdinburghOlderWeaver2026">[https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up Grant, Register of Apprentices of Edinburgh (1906), printed p.71: James, father Robert, Wester Duddingston, William Sclaitter, 16 June 1641; printed page re-read]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 Watson, Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses (1929), printed p.208 (PDF p.218): James the weaver, 20 June 1649, matching Sclaitter and 16 June 1641 apprenticeship]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_internments_~_greyfriars_churchyard_1658-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=268 Henry Paton (ed.),Register of interments in Greyfriars,1658–1700(1902),printed pp.196,252; PDF pp.212,268]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson,Register of Edinburgh Apprentices,1666–1700(1929),p.37]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson,Register of Edinburgh Apprentices1666–1700(1929),printed p.37]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=277 Henry Paton (ed.), Edinburgh marriages 1595–1700, printed p.267/PDF p.277: Bessie Whyte 6 July 1649; Agnes Duncan 11 November 1653; maintained printed-register review reused]. The 1696 entry omits a death qualification; silence does not prove that father alive. A cancelled cordiner apprenticeship followed by an apothecary apprenticeship six years later is compatible with one man, although not established. The matching apprentice/father names and father’s weaving trade support testing that possibility; burgess status is given only for the 1696 father and the two masters differ. Keep the two existing profiles distinct pending an identifier; do not create them again. This alternative limits the father assessment rather than being erased.

His Whitecastle adult occurrence in 1672 makes a 1696 first apprenticeship less ordinary, and no trade or residence bridge identifies him; retain him as a weaker compatible comparison. The proposed father of Whitecastle James is unchanged. Other Edinburgh James households remain comparisons, without unproved mergers, sibling transfers or replacement birth dates.

  on 5 May 1655;<ref name="RobertBaptism">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms,
  1564–1950,” database, FamilySearch,
  [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRSV-T1T Robert Glasgow],
  baptised 5 May 1655, Edinburgh, son of James Glasgow and Agnes Duncan.</ref>
* [[Glasgow-3143|Marion Glasgow]], daughter of Agnes Duncan;
* [[Glasgow-1373|Bethia Glasgow]], daughter of Agnes Duncan; and
* [[Glasgow-1057|John Glasgow]], son of Agnes Duncan.

The individual baptism entries should be consulted for the evidence naming
each child's mother.

Marion married William Calder at Edinburgh on 29 June 1686.<ref name="MarionMarriage">Paton, ''Register of Marriages for the Parish of
Edinburgh'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/register_of_marriages_for_the_parish_of_edinburgh_1595-1700_~_1898.pdf#page=278
printed p. 268].</ref> On the following day William was admitted as a burgess
through his wife Marion, explicitly described as a daughter of James Glasgow,
weaver and burgess.<ref name="CalderBurgess">Watson, ''Roll of Edinburgh
Burgesses'', [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=101
printed p. 91].</ref>

James's date and place of death have not been identified. He was alive on 18
October 1693.<ref name="Master1693" />

=== Birth and parentage ===

The former birth date of 19 March 1626 and birthplace of Inveresk belong to
[[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]], son of [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]] and
[[Clerk-296|Jannet Clerk]], not to this man.<ref name="InvereskBaptism">“Scotland,
Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, FamilySearch,
[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-GQW James Glasgow], baptised 19
March 1626, Inveresk and Musselburgh.</ref>

The apprenticeship directly names this James's father as Robert Glasgow,
servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston.<ref name="Apprentice1641" /> [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]] is a plausible
profile match, but the record does not prove that identity; preserve the
relationship as uncertain. The record does not name James's mother.
[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]] is an uncertain working attachment only.

[[Glasgow-1376|James Glasgow]] is not supported as a son born on 29 January
1657. The cited event is the baptism of Marion Glasgow and names James as her
father; it is not a birth record for a son James.

=== Probable later sons ===

On 22 April 1696 a James Glasgow, son of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess, was
apprenticed to William Adam, apothecary and burgess. On 11 October 1699 Thomas,
youngest son of James Glasgow, weaver and burgess, was apprenticed to James
Affleck, baxter and burgess.<ref name="LaterSons">Henry Paton, ed.,
[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf
''Register of Apprentices of the City of Edinburgh, 1666–1700''] (Scottish
Record Society, 1929), printed p. 37.</ref>

The exact name, trade, burgess status and city, together with James's 1693
master entry, make this profile the probable identity of their father. Neither
entry names a mother, however, and the late chronology warrants uncertain
attachments until a baptism, testament or incorporation record adds a second
identifier.

The 7 May 1690 apprentice James was a different person: his father was already
deceased and was a weaver at Lindsayland.<ref name="LaterSons" />

Priority records are James's burial or testament; baptisms or incorporation
papers for the 1696 James and 1699 Thomas; and evidence that identifies Robert
Glasgow of Wester Duddingston. [[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow]], husband of
[[Clerk-460|Helen Clerk]], is a separate same-name man.
</blockquote>


=== Duddingston father assessment — 17 October 2026 ===

[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow of Duddingston]] is now assessed as the probable father of [[Glasgow-1150|James Glasgow, Edinburgh weaver]], the Edinburgh weaver. Grant’s 16 June 1641 apprenticeship names James’s father Robert and places the entry at Wester Duddingston with William Crichtoun and master William Sclaitter. The 20 June 1649 burgess admission repeats Sclaitter’s name and the exact apprenticeship date, securely connecting the recorded son to the adult weaver. The Robert buried at Duddingston on 17 January 1647 fits the father’s name, parish and preceding generation, six years after the apprenticeship and before James’s independent household began in 1649. Taken together, the specific local father and the Duddingston burial favour one Robert over an otherwise unattested second contemporary Robert in that parish. The previous assessment treated the lack of a unique identifier as a reason to stop at plausible; the combined argument warrants probable, while remaining an inference.

The apprenticeship proves James’s father was Robert; identifying that father with the burial account [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow of Duddingston]] is probable rather than documented. The burial index gives no age, son, wife or occupation, and burial in the parish does not itself prove residence at Wester Duddingston. A second local Robert remains possible. The two craft entries are a linked identity chain, not two independent statements naming the father. The exact scope of “servitor” in the printed apprenticeship wording need not decide the inference: the entry supplies the father’s name and Duddingston association. No mother is identified, so Deborah Ivey is not upgraded. Robert’s unsupported Archibald-1097 ancestry and his compatible identification with Andrew-3163’s recorded son Robert-4006 remain separate questions. Neither the later Fisherrow sasine identity nor the Edinburgh weaver’s possible Lindsaylands continuation is needed for this father conclusion.

This is a stronger local assessment of an existing father, not a new attachment, newly found source or live WikiTree save. The fixed pre-1850 working tree has 63 retained profiles below James and 972 on the other side of this edge; 61,236 connected pairs depend on it. These overlapping branch-impact counts measure priority, not a probability or 63 independently verified people. Working family membership and confidently marked connectivity are unchanged because probable remains below the confident grades. The prior effective uncertain flag, ungraded local assessment and plausible narrative are preserved. The printed 1641 apprenticeship page was re-read for this review; the burgess and burial citations use the maintained earlier source reviews, with the burial seen as an index rather than the original register. [https://glasgow.phenotype.dev/branches/early-scottish-records/#duddingston-probable-father Confidence review and source limits]. <ref>Combined existing family evidence: [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso28scotuoft/page/71/mode/2up Grant, Register of Apprentices of Edinburgh (1906), printed p.71: James, father Robert, Wester Duddingston, William Sclaitter, 16 June 1641; printed page re-read]; [https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/roll_of_edinburgh_burgesses_1406_to_1700.pdf#page=218 Watson, Roll of Edinburgh Burgesses (1929), printed p.208 (PDF p.218): James the weaver, 20 June 1649, matching Sclaitter and 16 June 1641 apprenticeship]; [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ NRS Duddingston OPR deaths/burials 684/60/47: Robert Glasgow, 17 January 1647; indexed citation, original image not inspected for this review]. The printed apprenticeship page was re-read; other source reviews retain their stated scope. The burial-register image was not inspected for this review.</ref>



=== Previous father assessment — superseded 17 October 2026 ===

The earlier possible/uncertain wording is retained as assessment history; the probable local assessment above replaces it.

<blockquote>
'''[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]]''' is a plausible existing-profile match for this father because of the Wester Duddingston association and chronology. The record does not, however, contain enough information to prove that the named father and the existing profile represent the same man. That relationship should therefore remain uncertain.
</blockquote>


=== Birth ===

The former birth date of 19 March 1626 and birthplace of Inveresk do not belong to this James.

The only presently supported birth statement is that James was born before 16 June 1641, when he entered his apprenticeship.<ref name="Apprentice1641" />

His birthplace remains unknown.

=== Parentage ===

The apprenticeship record directly identifies James's father as '''Robert Glasgow, servant to William Crichtoun in Wester Duddingston'''.<ref name="Apprentice1641" />

'''[[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]]''' is now the probable father-profile match on the combined Duddingston burial, apprenticeship and burgess evidence. The named father is direct; identification with the burial account remains inferred. The live WikiTree father flag remains uncertain.

The record does not name James's mother.

'''[[Ivey-2264|Deborah Ivey]]''' is not identified as his mother in any inspected record. Any attachment should remain uncertain and be treated as a working hypothesis rather than an established relationship.

=== Distinct from the Inveresk James ===

This James was not '''[[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]]''', who was baptised at Inveresk and Musselburgh on 19 March 1626 as a son of [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Clerk-296|Jannet Clerk]].<ref name="InvereskBaptism">“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950,” database, ''FamilySearch'', James Glasgow, baptised 19 March 1626, Inveresk and Musselburgh, son of Alexander Glasgow, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-GQW record VQ4V-GQW] (accessed 2025).</ref>

The 1641 apprenticeship names Robert Glasgow, not Alexander Glasgow, as the father of the Edinburgh weaver. The two men should remain on separate profiles.

=== Incorrect child profile ===

'''[[Glasgow-1376|James Glasgow]]''' is not a supported child of this family and should not be attached as a son born on 29 January 1657.

The cited record for that date is the baptism of Marion Glasgow and names James Glasgow as her father. It is not a birth or baptism record for a son named James.

=== Identity caution ===

This James should not be confused with '''[[Glasgow-3077|James Glasgow]]''', who married [[Clerk-460|Helen Clerk]] and was associated with [[Glasgow-3093|John Glasgow]].

The Edinburgh weaver is identified by:

* the 1641 apprenticeship naming him as a son of Robert Glasgow;
* his apprenticeship to William Sclaitter;
* his 1649 admission as an Edinburgh burgess;
* his occupation as a weaver;
* his marriages to Bessie Whyte and Agnes Duncan; and
* the 1686 burgess record identifying Marion Glasgow as his daughter.

=== Further research ===

Useful remaining records include:

* the original apprenticeship papers or incorporation records;
* records establishing whether [[Glasgow-1156|Robert Glasgow]] was the father named in the apprenticeship;
* records identifying James's mother;
* original baptism entries for each child;
* any further records establishing the children's mothers;
* a burial or testament for James;
* records identifying James's birthplace; and
* further records concerning William Calder and Marion Glasgow.

=== Possible Fisherrow property appearances, 1646–1647 ===

A James Glasgow described as a weaver appears in the Edinburgh particular sasine index with [[Glasgow-1148|Alexander Glasgow]] in Fischerraw, burgess of Musselburgh. Their shared references are 33/258, recorded 14 February 1646; 33/360, recorded 15 May 1646; and 34/287, recorded 10 February 1647. Edward Glasgow also shares 33/258.<ref name="EarlyFisherrow1646">Scottish Record Office, Indexes no.44 (1958), Edinburgh etc. register of sasines 1644–1653, printed pp.159–160; RS25 33/258, recorded 14 February 1646; 33/360, 15 May 1646; 34/287, 10 February 1647; printed columns visually inspected 15 October 2026, original instruments unread; [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015072481222&seq=167].</ref> Some references recur on the next printed page; those repetitions are not extra events. The adjacent 16 June 1646 date is Isobel Givan’s, not Alexander’s.

The documented Edinburgh weaver is the leading possible identity for this indexed James: trade, regional setting and the interval between his 1641 apprenticeship and 1649 burgess admission fit. The index itself does not give James’s own residence, father, spouse or role in the instrument. Alexander’s son [[Glasgow-3923|James Glasgow]], baptised at Inveresk in 1626, is a real rival; his father Alexander differs from this weaver’s apprenticeship-proved father Robert of Wester Duddingston. [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]], the earlier Fisherrow tailor, could have changed trade. [[Glasgow-3332|James Glasgow]], associated tentatively with the later Lindsaylands weaver, is a weaker comparison whose estimated birth is not a hard exclusion. [[Glasgow-3910|James Glasgow of Quothquan]] had died by 1624 and cannot be a living party in 1646, though an unread deed could mention a deceased predecessor. The instruments, not repeated index references, must decide capacity and kinship.
